sections.overview: The Baikal omul is a whitefish endemic to Lake Baikal and its tributaries, historically also called Coregonus autumnalis migratorius.
sections.identification: It is a pelagic, schooling member of the salmon family; the sources consulted do not establish a single field mark that reliably separates all populations.
sections.habitat: It feeds and grows in the lake, using different depths with season and food availability, then enters tributary rivers to reproduce.
sections.diet: Its principal food is the endemic zooplankton Epischura baikalensis, supplemented by small fish and other invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Spawning migrants enter rivers in autumn, and the fish is also an important prey of the Baikal seal.
sections.reproduction: It spawns over gravelly river riffles; eggs develop through winter and newly hatched fish drift back toward the lake in spring.
sections.ecology: This lake-and-river life cycle links pelagic feeding grounds with tributary spawning habitat and the lake’s native predator, the Baikal seal.
sections.conservation: The cited global assessment classifies it as Least Concern, while fisheries management still monitors the lake’s spawning runs and catches.
